status: read-only implementation plan; no source, renderer, builder or assets modified

pipeline_findings.finding: Legacy all-corpus preparer reads outputs/odia-cinema-series/*-report.json, stages old PDFs, and replaces cinema.json with only parts/articles/books. Do not run it for sequential prose updates: it would discard review_books, archived_review_books and newer top-level data, and assumes all old preview reports exist.

cinemaArticle(entry) renders a single source synchronously with current route map, credits, notes, language spans and related links. This is the fast existing validation entrance; fresh Node process required after edits because imported JSON is cached.

Reads site cinema.json and canonical source paths directly, plus book-narrative plan. Existing preface/part intros/selected bridges/callouts/guide/timeline give breathing room. No line-art slot schema exists.

--layout-only still constructs all chapters and writes the named PDF before exiting after page-map; it is not a cheap per-chapter preview. Use isolated --revision suffix for any proof, never current reviewed edition suffix.

Final run renders every page and contact sheet; do this once after prose/image lock, not once per article. Printed chapter-page references require a layout pass followed by final build with --page-map and stability assertion.

algorithm: Read canonical manifest and existing cinema.json; resolve one unique slug in both.

Read frontmatter and body without rewriting source. Copy only reviewed title, description, series_intro, author/status/research_date if those fields exist in the existing data contract; calculate SHA256 from actual unchanged source bytes.
Preserve route, image objects/derivatives/provenance, focal positions, hero, all other article entries, parts and all current/archive book metadata. Do not rebuild image derivatives for prose edits.
Fail if declared hero path or Markdown image set changed: asset integration needs separate explicit scope.
Report old/new hash and changed metadata fields; default dry-run. Write only the targeted cinema.json entry on --apply. Root owns canonical manifest synchronization and narrative-plan adaptations.

Run cinemaArticle on the updated in-memory entry; assert no duplicate IDs/unresolved local footnote targets, mandatory credit notes preserved and no raw KB links. Save per-slug rendered HTML plus source/plan hashes in draft outputs.
proposed_targeted_metadata_updater.warning: No suitable safe targeted updater found in inspected current tools; this is a proposed helper, not an existing command.

fast_sequential_review: Root revises one canonical article; record source hash and independent prose/source-budget review before next article.

Use one fresh Node process importing cinemaArticle to render the active slug and run paragraph/footnote/link/image-preservation checks. Review resulting HTML as a fragment, not proof of full Astro/CSS appearance.

After initial local Astro development environment is prepared, a coordinator may keep one local dev session for on-demand route views; do not rerun npm build per article. Do not start a server or bypass any browser restriction as part of this plan.
Run targeted semantic/unit tests only when renderer/layout behavior changes; no repeated full suite for prose-only edits.

After all articles lock, synchronize narrative overview opening/companion and section_map hashes, exact heading callout targets, bridges/guide note IDs and metadata once. Final site build and final digital/print book production then validate the entire corpus.

line_art_design.purpose: Sparse pauses that carry a particular literary connection, not a decoration repeated after every chapter.
line_art_design.quantity: Propose three or four unique pieces across seven parts, selected after prose sequence is clear; no new obligatory blank part leaves.
line_art_design.proposed_schema: book-narrative.line_art: [{id, after_slug OR before_part_id, path, width_pt, max_height_pt, alt, caption, provenance_path, decorative}]
line_art_design.placement: Render between completed chapter text/bridge and next chapter opener, or inside first chapter after part intro if sufficient room. Small 80–160pt wide and roughly40–80pt high; fit-or-omit optional decorative instance rather than forcing a nearly blank leaf. Never replace a hero or required image credit.
line_art_design.accessibility: If purely decorative, web alt empty and no focusable wrapper; meaningful scenes need short descriptive alt. Existing documentary/source credits stay in ordinary numbered notes. Rights-bearing new work requires provenance and any required credit.
line_art_design.asset_requirements: User-approved unique restrained line art; no generated images in this task. Any future generation follows Human Natural/imagegen instructions, original retained, no bitmap editing through unrelated tools.
line_art_design.web_scope: Optional restrained inter-part illustration on hub only if useful; do not automatically insert ornaments into all 41 article pages. Modern Web Guidance search/retrieve required before frontend implementation.
line_art_design.book_layout: Keep 11pt/16.5 body, existing full natural hero placements,6x9 margins/fonts/covers. Use measured flowables and small CondPageBreak thresholds; avoid broad KeepTogether around long prose and avoid universal font reduction.

book_environment.legacy_dependency_path: Builder prepends sibling prahallad-nataka-research/tmp/pdfs/deps; inspect availability/version before final run rather than silently changing shaping runtime.
book_environment.fonts: tools/cinema-book/fonts/SourceSerif4-{Regular,Bold,It,BoldIt}.ttf and existing Noto Serif Oriya; mixed-run shaping fix must remain.
book_environment.caution: If page map not stable, repeat only required print layout/final pass. One final production cycle may legitimately need these multipass operations; do not promise one invocation.
book_environment.publication_gates: Only when separately authorized: build:coast, test:coast, build:publication and disclosure/budget checks. No publication implied by draft recomposition.
